documents_expected.why: call page: who can apply, what is funded
Terms of Reference: proponents, ineligible activities, reporting, payments

eligibility.rule: Registered non-profit, local government or First Nation (others through a partner)
eligibility.quote: Proponents must be a registered non-profit organization, local government, or First Nations Band. Unqualified groups or organizations may partner with a qualified organization.
alt_quotes: Applications are accepted from the following: Registered non-profit organizations; First Nations; Local governments.

eligibility.rule: Project in the Fund Service Area (Columbia Valley)
eligibility.quote: Projects must be in the Fund Service Area.

eligibility.rule: Addresses an IUCN threat to biodiversity in a theme area
eligibility.quote: Projects must address IUCN threats to biodiversity targets and fall into at least one theme area (see Section 4).
Not the existing obligation or responsibility of the federal, provincial or local governments;

eligibility.rule: No capacity building or operating costs
eligibility.quote: Capacity building or operating expenses for organizations;

eligibility.rule: Multi-year projects up to three years, approved yearly
eligibility.quote: Multi-year projects are acceptable to a maximum of three years.

after_award.quote: Proponents must be prepared to make a 10-minute presentation on the outcomes of their work on an annual basis, in addition to submitting a written report.

notes: The 2027 general intake is closed and under review; no application form or guide is published, so the document list is unknown and coverage is incomplete. Land acquisition and covenant applications are taken any time by contact. 25% of the grant is paid on the approved final report. Partnerships with other funders get priority but aren't required. The ToR's cover page is an image (a low_text block).
